steps.content: [Flashback]

<size=45>July 12, N.F. 115 19:48

Operation BR-005 commences in...</size>
12 days 19 hours 59 minutes
Are we there yet? This Black Tide you mentioned?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: We're almost there. The Black Tide isn't far from Euphoria, but given your current state... are you sure about this? That "Black Tide" is actually a liquid contamination zone, a leftover from past campaigns. Going in will only make your condition worse. We could place you somewhere safer instead.
You're the ones who told me this contamination zone might hold buried Rancors... How sure are you about that?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Your guess is as good as mine. Over two hundred observers were stationed there, but none survived after the contamination erupted. DisCity never heard from a single one of them again.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: If I must give an estimate... thirty percent?
You knew what Augustus had been searching for all these years—those scattered weapons she called "old friends." It was her sensing the Rancors' presence that brought the Broken Blade squad here.
Now, your hands clutched the porthole, trembling under the increasing weight of the Black Ring.
That's enough. Thirty percent is plenty.
Any advantage could tip the scales and increase my chances of bringing her back... I can't stop now. Not when we're this close.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: But that thirty percent I gave you? That's our chance of getting out of the Black Tide alive.
No sooner had those words been spoken than Scarface burst through the cabin door, completely out of breath.

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: Man, this is nuts! We're... bleurgh... the Black Tide!

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: Here we are!
[Deck]

A churning black sea stretched before you, its surface alive with the writhing of massive shadows and the flicker of monstrous silhouettes. The air reeked of decay and rusted metal. Each wave slammed against the hull, groaning the warship's steel frame.

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: Talk about a warm welcome—bleurgh!

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Keep your breakfast down. It is strange, though. Those city-states' tech back then shouldn't have been capable of creating contamination on this scale.

The swells, black and several meters high, wrapped around the ship like living things, tilting the deck at a frightening angle. Surrounded by the roaring tide, you raised your voices just to be heard.
Is Augustus aware of the situation here?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Well, she knows now. I just got her message—
All units, clear the contamination and advance at full speed! To the heart of the Black Tide!

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: BLEURGH—!

Scarface vomited over the rail, then crushed a writhing creature that had crawled aboard and hurled it back into the sea. A trail of foul slime sprayed across the deck, releasing a putrid, fishy stench.
What are these things?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Tide Crawlers. Hold on tight!

Another wave hurled the ship into the air. For a weightless moment, it hung at its apex before crashing back down. The impact threw everyone from their feet, and as the crew slammed onto the deck, massive waves engulfed the vessel, trying to drag you all into the consuming dark.

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: Bleurgh— Filthy bugs stewing in black water! Back off, you freaks! Don't touch me!

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: You heard the General! Straight into the Black Tide! Let's move—

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Get back here! Forget about moving out. We've got a bigger problem on our hands...

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: We've lost the advisor.
[Underwater] [Bubbling sounds]

The black waves swallowed you whole, tearing you from the others despite your desperate struggles. Shadowy forms brushed against you in the depths, their gnawing teeth and clawing grips tearing at your skin and clothes.
A crushing weight filled your lungs, and a dizzying blackness encroached on your vision until consciousness slipped away. When you finally forced your eyes open...
You were clinging to a piece of driftwood, alone in the vast, empty ocean.
Ow!
You take a single step up the stairs, and your face instantly contorts into a pained grimace.
You had woken to a searing ache in every muscle this morning.
The small cabin at the base of the lighthouse remains dim, the hearth fire that sheltered you through the night having burned out hours ago, not long after you fell asleep.
The thunderstorm has passed. No monsters scratch at the door; only the rhythmic crash of ocean waves remains. Through the small porthole, a faint light filters down from an overcast sky.
Leaning heavily on the wall, you limp around the cramped space. No medical supplies. No water. No food. Your only option is the staircase, leading to who knows where.
Judging by the design of the equipment here, this place must have once belonged to DisCity...
A sharp twist of pain in your stomach makes the stairs blur and double. Your hand braced against the wall trembles uncontrollably.
Heh. Looks like I barely have the strength left to talk to myself...
But talking to yourself is your last resort, the only way to keep your mind sober. With each whispered word, you force one leg forward, then the other, continuing the climb.
The age of this place and the lighthouse observatory... they both match Broken Blade's intel. That woman from last night... she has to know something.

Could the Rancors be here? But that woman never returned after storming out last night. Does she not need to eat or sleep? Unless she was just a figment of your imagination... unless you actually died in the Black Tide.
No... Get a grip. Don't go down that road.
A fresh wave of pain yanks you back to reality. You haul your other leg up onto the next step. Above you stretches a seemingly endless spiral of stairs.
There may be no survival supplies up there, but you know something far more important awaits—
The beacon. Its light, cutting through the sea fog, would be the clearest distress signal you could send. Your best chance to contact your team. Your only shot at extraction.
I need to rendezvous with the team first...
[White Flash] [Flying Knife]
Your words are cut short by the whistle of metal slicing the air. A knife flies past your ear, embedding itself in the wall ahead, stopping your path mere inches from your face.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Get out!
You know that commanding voice. You don't need to look to know who it belongs to.
You're still alive too. Lucky, aren't we?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Are you deaf? I said get out.
I didn't come up here for the view. I need water, food, antibiotics. Point me to them, and I'm gone. I won't touch a thing.
She acts as if you aren't even there. Gritting your teeth, you force patience into your voice and speak again.
Look, I apologize for the interruption... but I'm dying.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: My congratulations.
The control room's up there, right? This is a rescue facility, not your private property. If you won't help, I'll activate the beacon myself.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: A nameless bastard has no right to touch the lighthouse.
Isn't a lighthouse meant to guide the lost? Right now, that's me.
You refuse to yield, taking another deliberate step forward—
Shing! A blade blurs through the air, severing a few loose strands of your hair before whistling back to its master's hand.
[Big CG: First Encounter]

You finally see her clearly, for the first time. Her frame is pure muscle, sculpted by brutal training, and her skin is rough from sea winds, a canvas for scars of every depth. But it's the look on her face that strikes deepest: a weary, unbridled ferocity.
Why are you so desperate to keep me away? What are you hiding?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: You. Have. No. Right. Is that simple enough for you?
Then give me food and water.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: There isn't any. Just die.
You're all talk. Go ahead, do it.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: I won't dirty my hands.
A disbelieving laugh escapes you. Her stubbornness would be admirable if it weren't so fatal.
Fine... We'll do this the hard way.
